requirement: Consent: guardian grants scoped, time-limited consent; Rewards: first grant rewards the guardian
why_critical: this is the core guardian action; the reward must go to the guardian (msg.sender), never to the requester, because the menu shows the guardian's balance.
expected: Register owner/requester, attest a record, then assert grant expiry, ConsentGranted and a reward minted to the granting guardian.

requirement: Consent: duration is 1-365 whole days
why_critical: consent must be time-limited to at most a year, and a missing uint256 cast would make every grant of 195+ days revert.
expected: Reject 0, 366 and 65535 days; accept 1, 194, 195 and 365 days with exact expiry (195+ catches the uint24 overflow).

requirement: Consent: an active duplicate grant is rejected
why_critical: silently extending an active grant, or re-minting on it, would let a guardian farm rewards or change terms without a revoke.
expected: An already-active tuple cannot be re-granted (not even one second before expiry) or rewarded again.

requirement: Consent: only the owner can change its own consent
why_critical: consent belongs to the guardian; no other guardian, requester or outsider may revoke or alter it.
expected: Separate owners: a caller can only create or revoke consent keyed to its own wallet.

requirement: Consent: a grant needs registered parties and a supported scope
why_critical: consent must name a real, registered requester; granting to an unregistered address or an unknown scope is a user error, not a grant. Any extra precondition would make the real contract drift from Python's fake chain unnoticed.
expected: Grants need both parties registered and a supported scope, and nothing more: a guardian may name its own wallet as requester.

requirement: Consent/Audit: exact requester and scope; denied attempts are logged
why_critical: consent is for an exact requester and scope; the audit log must record denied attempts, including the raw scope the audit view prints.
expected: Wrong requester, wrong scope and unsupported scopes (0, 3 and 255) give a false result and a persistent denied AccessAttempt (no revert); the raw scope 3 is logged, and checkAccess agrees for scope 0.

requirement: Audit/integrity: unregistered parties or missing evidence are denied and logged
why_critical: an attacker with no identity, or a record that was never attested, must be refused, and the refusal must still be auditable.
expected: Each missing prerequisite (unregistered requester, unregistered owner, owner without evidence) creates a denied event and no token movement.

requirement: Consent: consent is invalid at the exact expiry timestamp
why_critical: expiry is exclusive (valid while now < expiresAt); an off-by-one would give a requester one extra block of access.
expected: At expiresAt - 1 access is allowed; at exactly expiresAt it is denied Expired (checkAccess and requestAccess agree).

requirement: Consent: revocation at any time, safe to repeat
why_critical: the guardian must be able to withdraw consent at any time, and repeating the action must be safe for the menu.
expected: Revoke emits ConsentRevoked and blocks access; a second revoke is a silent no-op; never-granted reverts; expired-but-not-revoked can still be revoked.

requirement: Audit/integrity: a changed or missing local record is denied
why_critical: this is the integrity check: a modified or unreadable local file must never be released, and the denial must be logged.
expected: A wrong (tampered) or zero observedHash is denied HashMismatch (7) in the one emitted event; the correct hash is allowed.

requirement: Audit: every access attempt is logged and moves no tokens
why_critical: access must be auditable every time and must not move tokens, otherwise reading data could be used to farm rewards.
expected: A valid request returns (true, Allowed) and emits the allowed event; every call is logged; no reward is minted and balances do not change.

requirement: Rewards: revoke and regrant gives no second reward
why_critical: toggling consent must not farm rewards, and a regrant must fully clear the revoked flag (the demo's final EXPIRED step depends on it).
expected: Grant, revoke and regrant: the regrant emits ConsentGranted with the new expiry, checkAccess is Allowed, getConsent shows revoked == false and a new expiry, and the tuple keeps exactly one lifetime reward.

requirement: Rewards: expiry and regrant gives no second reward
why_critical: expiry is the other way a tuple becomes re-grantable; it must follow the same one-lifetime-reward rule as revocation.
expected: Grant, let it expire, regrant: ConsentGranted carries the new expiry, access is allowed again, but no second reward.

requirement: Rewards: one lifetime reward per (owner, requester, scope)
why_critical: shows the reward key is (owner, requester, scope), matching the demo balances: school 0 -> 1, doctor 1 -> 2.
expected: A different requester or scope for the same owner, or a different owner, earns its own single reward (the key is the full tuple); hasReceivedReward tracks scope-2 tuples as well as scope-1 ones.

requirement: Rewards: grant and mint are atomic
why_critical: grant and reward are one atomic transaction; a failed mint must not leave a half-done grant that looks successful, and a try/catch that swallows the failure would fail here.
expected: With an unconfigured reward token, the grant reverts as a whole with the token's own NotMinter error (bubbled up unchanged, so the menu names the misconfiguration): no consent, no rewarded flag, access still NoConsent.

requirement: Interface: denial precedence matches Python
why_critical: Python's fake chain and messages assume this exact order (UnsupportedScope, NotRegistered, MissingEvidence, NoConsent, Revoked, Expired, then hash); this is the only test that pins it on the real contract, and the audit view prints the logged reason.
expected: Denial precedence: several failing conditions at once always yield the documented reason, in the event and in checkAccess; a wrong or zero observedHash never replaces an earlier denial (NoConsent, MissingEvidence, Revoked, Expired).

requirement: Interface: reason codes are frozen at 0-7
why_critical: Python names reasons from plain integers; a reordered enum would still pass name-based checks but print the wrong reason in the demo.
expected: The Reason enum values are frozen at 0-7 in the order app/models.py uses.

requirement: Deployment: the manager is wired to real contracts
why_critical: a manager wired to a wallet instead of the real registry or token would accept or deny access on garbage data.
expected: The constructor rejects zero and non-contract dependency addresses; a zero address is reported before a wallet (ZeroAddress, then NotAContract).

requirement: Full workflow: the demo storyline works on-chain
why_critical: shows the unit-tested rules compose into the scripted demonstration, in the step order of docs/DEMO.md (steps 2-7) and of integration/demo_workflow.py. The allowed requests after the tamper and after the regrant are extra checks here; the demo checks the original locally and does not request before expiry.
expected: The full demo storyline on-chain in docs/DEMO.md order: deny, grant/reward, allow, doctor grant, tamper deny while the doctor grant is active (original still verifies), revoke deny, regrant 1 day (no reward), exact expiry deny.

requirement: Interface: revert order matches the Python error messages
why_critical: the menu prints the bare error name and Python's fake chain raises in this order, so a different order would show the guardian a different "rejected: <Name>" on the real node than in the Python tests.
expected: Revert order with several failing conditions at once: grantConsent checks UnsupportedScope, then InvalidDuration, then NotRegistered, then ConsentStillActive; revokeConsent checks UnsupportedScope before NoConsentToRevoke.

requirement: Gas: a revoke or a first grant writes no new storage slot
why_critical: gas is a measured result, and writing a storage slot from zero costs about 20,000 gas. With the fields in separate slots, every revoke would cost about 19,000 gas more and every first grant about 24,000 more.
expected: A tuple's expiresAt, revoked and rewarded fields share one storage slot: a first grant, a revoke and a regrant each write only that slot, and getConsent and hasReceivedReward still read every field back.

requirement: Rewards: stated limitation, rewards are limited per tuple only
why_critical: this pins the real bound (2k^2 units from k wallets, no vaccination record needed), not just one self-reward per scope. It stays harmless for access because access never reads a balance (SOL-RT-05).
expected: Stated limitation: the (owner, requester, scope) tuple is the only reward limit. Three registered wallets with no attested record mint 2 * 3 * 3 = 18 units by granting each other, and themselves, both scopes; regrants after expiry add none, and the units open no record.

requirement: Registration/clinic: a wallet binds to one nonzero identity commitment
why_critical: every consent and access check starts from "is this wallet registered", so registration must bind the hash to msg.sender.
expected: Register a nonzero identity hash from one wallet; assert the registered flag (derived from the nonzero hash), the stored hash and the UserRegistered event.

requirement: Registration/clinic: duplicate and zero registrations are rejected
why_critical: a second registration could swap a wallet's identity after consents were granted; a zero hash is not a commitment.
expected: Prove duplicate registration and zero hashes are rejected without corrupting previous state.

requirement: Registration/clinic: only the trusted clinic attests a vaccination
why_critical: the vaccination commitment is the evidence every access is checked against; only the trusted issuer may create it. A tx.origin check would let any contract the clinic's wallet calls attest in its name.
expected: Use distinct clinic and attacker callers; only the configured clinic may attest, judged by msg.sender (a call whose tx.origin is the clinic is still rejected).

requirement: Registration/clinic: evidence needs a registered guardian and is frozen
why_critical: frozen evidence means a later (possibly tampered) file can never replace the attested commitment.
expected: Reject unregistered guardians, zero record hashes and overwriting frozen evidence.

requirement: Data minimisation: the read API and the events expose commitments only
why_critical: the chain is public, so reads and logs must expose references only, never identity or health plaintext.
expected: The read API and the registry events carry only fixed-size commitments: getUserInfo returns three static words (flag and two bytes32), and each event carries one bytes32 of data plus indexed addresses.

requirement: Audit/integrity: lookups of unregistered accounts never revert
why_critical: ConsentManager and the Python menu call getUserInfo for unregistered parties; a revert would erase the denied AccessAttempt event.
expected: getUserInfo on a fresh address returns (false, 0, 0) without reverting; registered non-guardians and unattested guardians have vaccinationHash 0.

requirement: Registration/clinic: the trusted clinic is fixed at deployment
why_critical: with a zero clinic nobody could ever attest, and the trusted issuer must be fixed at deployment, not chosen later.
expected: The constructor rejects a zero clinic and stores the configured clinic.

requirement: Interface: revert order matches the Python error messages
why_critical: the menu prints the bare error name, so a wrong actor must always see "rejected: NotTrustedClinic" whatever else is wrong.
expected: Revert order: attestation checks NotTrustedClinic, then NotRegistered, then ZeroHash, then EvidenceAlreadyRegistered; registration checks ZeroHash before AlreadyRegistered.

requirement: Registration/clinic: stated limitation, a commitment identifies no one on its own
why_critical: registration binds a commitment to a wallet, not to a person, so it is neither identity proof nor Sybil resistance. A uniqueness check would not help: a fresh salt gives a fresh commitment.
expected: Stated limitation: identity commitments are not unique across wallets. A second wallet may register a copy of another wallet's public commitment; both stay registered with the same hash, and the copy gains no evidence.

requirement: Rewards: the minter is set once, by the deployer, to a contract
why_critical: whoever is minter controls all rewards, so setup must be a one-shot deployer action that points at a contract, never at a person. Only msg.sender counts: a tx.origin check would let any contract the deployer's wallet calls choose the minter.
expected: Reject a wrong caller (also one whose tx.origin is the deployer), zero and non-contract minters, and a second configuration, in the order NotDeployer, MinterAlreadySet, ZeroAddress, NotAContract; the deployer configures exactly once.

requirement: Rewards: only the configured ConsentManager can mint
why_critical: if anyone but ConsentManager could mint, rewards would no longer prove a real consent grant.
expected: Nobody can mint before setup; afterwards guardian, requester, attacker and even the deployer are rejected; only the configured minter succeeds.

requirement: Rewards: exactly one unit per mint
why_critical: one unit per call with no amount parameter means even the minter cannot inflate a single reward; the menu prints balanceOf as a plain integer.
expected: Each mint adds exactly one unit to the recipient and to total supply and emits RewardMinted(recipient, 1).

requirement: Rewards: no mint to the zero address
why_critical: a reward sent to address(0) would inflate supply with units nobody holds.
expected: Minting to the zero address is rejected and changes nothing; the minter check comes first, so a non-minter sees NotMinter.

requirement: Rewards: a token balance never authorizes access
why_critical: the design rule is "consent controls access, tokens are only rewards"; this proves the manager never consults balanceOf.
expected: A positive balance alone never grants access: a rewarded account without consent is denied, and a guardian's balance survives revocation while access does not.

requirement: Rewards: reward units are non-transferable
why_critical: reward units must be non-transferable so they cannot be sold or used to buy someone else's standing.
expected: The token exposes no transfer, transferFrom, approve or burn function: calls with those selectors fail.

requirement: Deployment: the deployer has setup authority only
why_critical: the deployer is an administrator, not a data owner; it must not be able to reward itself or redirect minting later.
expected: The deployer's only power is the one-time setup: it holds no balance and cannot mint or reconfigure afterwards.
